assembly_instructions: 1. Bolt base_plate to the floor plane, then fasten front_rail, back_rail, left_rail, and right_rail on top of it as the 8.6 m by 5.0 m datum frame. 2. Stand post_front_left, post_front_right, post_back_left, and post_back_right on the rails, then add x_brace_front, x_brace_back, x_brace_left, and x_brace_right so all elevated subassemblies have a visible load path. 3. Mount input_plate, training_data_pipe, and embedding_table at the base, then connect embedding_table to residual_pipe with embedding_bus. 4. Install residual_pipe vertically through the open central slot and add the eight visible split transformer layers plus layer_count_marker, layer_elision_rail, and layer_tick_* plates to show the 96-layer deep-narrow stack without hiding the pipe. 5. Attach the exploded attention subassembly on the viewer-left side of block_03_attn_half: attn_pre_norm, q_projection_rail, k_projection_rail, v_projection_rail, q_head_fanout, kv_head_bank, qk_norm_disk, rope_disk, attn_kernel, and attn_o_proj; connect it back to residual_pipe with attention_return_bus. 6. Mount the eight kv_cache_cell_* cartridges on kv_cache_bus and tie the cache bus to both kv_head_bank and attn_kernel so the 8 KV-head GQA reduction is visible. 7. Attach the exploded MoE subassembly on the viewer-right side of block_03_moe_half: ffn_post_norm, moe_router, moe_group_limit, moe_alltoall_dispatch, expert_arc_backplane, eight expert_group_* cartridges, eight active_expert_lane_* rails, routed_expert_count_comb, moe_shared_expert, moe_group_gemm, fp8_gemm_disk, moe_alltoall_combine, and moe_output_bus. 8. Fasten prediction_head_left and prediction_head_right above the final layer with prediction_bridge_bus, then add mtp_head, lm_loss, mtp_loss, mode_think, and mode_no_think on supported brackets. 9. Install optimizer_adamw, post_train_rl, and parallelism_marker on their support brackets and connect each to the main frame with named bus bars. 10. Verify that every elevated plate is connected to base_plate either through a rail/post or through a named compute bus, and that no explanatory subsystem is hidden inside an opaque enclosure.

info.summary: 355B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts language model from Zhipu AI / Z.ai (32B activated per token). Deep-and-narrow design: 96 layers × 5120 hidden dim. GQA attention (96 Q heads / 8 KV heads, partial RoPE, QK-Norm), 160 routed + 1 shared expert per layer with sigmoid loss-free routing and group-limited top-8 dispatch, MTP head for speculative decoding, and a hybrid thinking / non-thinking mode that shares weights. Pre-trained on ~23 T tokens, post-trained for agentic + reasoning + coding with self-distillation RL.
info.description: GLM-4.5 is Z.ai's flagship open MoE for the ARC trinity: agentic, reasoning, and coding. Compared with GLM-4 it is much sparser, with only 32B of 355B parameters activated per token; it is deeper at 96 layers and narrower at 5120 hidden dimension. Routing uses a sigmoid gate with auxiliary-loss-free balance bias and a group-limit constraint so each token may activate experts on at most four of eight device groups. QK-Norm plus partial RoPE mark the attention path, and a single Multi-Token Prediction head supports speculative decoding. Training is represented as a 23T-token curriculum followed by SFT and self-distillation RL, with FP8 GEMMs and BF16 master weights.

facts.label: group-limited routing
facts.value: At most 4 of 8 device groups per token

comparisons.delta: GLM-4.5 moves from dense GLM-4-class decoders to a sparse 355B MoE while keeping per-token activated compute around 32B parameters.
GLM-4.5 is smaller and deeper, uses GQA with partial RoPE and QK-Norm, and adds group-limited routing over eight expert groups.

parts.name: Right Side Cross Brace

parts.name: Input Tokens (BPE)
parts.role: Token-ID stream plate for the 151,552-token BPE vocabulary, feeding integer IDs into the embedding slab.
parts.bottleneck: Loader-side BPE throughput on the CPU.

parts.name: Token Stream Bead 1
parts.role: First visible token bead marks discrete BPE token IDs entering the embedding lookup.

parts.name: Token Stream Bead 2
parts.role: Second token bead shows the packed sequence moving toward the embedding table.

parts.name: Embedding (V=151K, d=5120)
parts.role: Token-embedding lookup slab tied to the LM head, representing about 776M parameters or 1.55 GiB in BF16.
parts.memory_footprint: 151K x 5120 x BF16 is about 1.55 GiB

parts.name: Embedding-to-Residual Bus
parts.role: Short vertical bus showing the first activation transfer from embedding space into the central residual stream.

parts.name: Residual Stream (d=5120, 96 layers)
parts.role: Central pre-norm residual stream carrying d=5120 activations through all 96 transformer layers in an exposed open slot.
parts.memory_footprint: B x T x d activations per layer
parts.algorithm: x = x + attn(rmsnorm_pre(x)); x = x + ffn(rmsnorm_post(x))

parts.name: Layer Count Spine: 96 Transformer Blocks
parts.role: Etched spine marks the unrendered layers 7 through 94 between the visible early and final split slices.
parts.bottleneck: Pipeline bubbles across 96 layers unless scheduled with 1F1B-style execution.

parts.name: 96-Layer Elision Rail
parts.role: Thin brass rail gives the omitted middle transformer layers a visible measured span beside the count spine.

parts.name: Layer Tick 16
parts.role: Tick plate marks the approximate sixteenth layer on the elided deep stack.

parts.name: Layer Tick 32
parts.role: Tick plate marks the approximate thirty-second layer on the elided deep stack.

parts.name: Layer Tick 48
parts.role: Tick plate marks the halfway point of the 96-layer transformer tower.

parts.name: Layer Tick 64
parts.role: Tick plate marks the approximate sixty-fourth layer on the elided deep stack.

parts.name: Layer Tick 80
parts.role: Tick plate marks the approximate eightieth layer before the final visible slices.

parts.name: Layer Tick 96
parts.role: Tick plate aligns with the final transformer slice and closes the 96-layer count.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 1 Attention Half
parts.role: First visible decoder attention half leaves a central slot open around the residual stream.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 1 MoE Half
parts.role: First visible decoder MoE half pairs with the attention half without covering the residual pipe.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 2 Attention Half
parts.role: Second visible decoder attention half repeats the deep-narrow layer pitch while exposing the center.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 2 MoE Half
parts.role: Second visible decoder MoE half shows the repeated sparse feed-forward side of the layer.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 3 Exploded Attention Half
parts.role: Third layer attention half is the exploded reference sublayer with its internals pulled outward on the left.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 3 Exploded MoE Half
parts.role: Third layer MoE half is the exploded reference feed-forward sublayer with its expert path pulled outward on the right.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 4 Attention Half
parts.role: Fourth visible attention half confirms the uniform 96-layer recipe without enclosing the pipe.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 4 MoE Half
parts.role: Fourth visible MoE half keeps the feed-forward side visible as a separate repeated slab.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 5 Attention Half
parts.role: Fifth visible attention half shows the lower stack before the elided middle layers.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 5 MoE Half
parts.role: Fifth visible MoE half preserves the visible left-right attention-to-expert decomposition.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 6 Attention Half
parts.role: Sixth visible attention half ends the lower rendered run before the layer-count gap.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 6 MoE Half
parts.role: Sixth visible MoE half precedes the elided middle layers on the count spine.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 95 Attention Half
parts.role: Penultimate attention half marks the upper end of the 96-layer stack after the elided middle span.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 95 MoE Half
parts.role: Penultimate MoE half shows that the sparse expert recipe continues through the high layers.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 96 Final Attention Half
parts.role: Final attention half feeds the tied LM head while leaving the residual pipe exposed.

parts.name: Transformer Slice 96 Final MoE Half
parts.role: Final MoE half completes the visible decoder stack before the tied vocabulary projection.

parts.name: Attention Pre-RMSNorm Gamma Plate
parts.role: Learned RMSNorm gamma plate normalizes the residual stream before QKV projection in each attention sublayer.
parts.memory_footprint: gamma is 5120 x BF16, about 10 KB per layer
parts.algorithm: x_hat = x / sqrt(mean(x*x) + eps); y = gamma * x_hat

parts.name: Q Projection Rail
parts.role: Copper rail carries normalized activations into the 96-query-head projection path.

parts.name: K Projection Rail
parts.role: Copper rail separates the key projection before it joins the compact 8-head KV bank.

parts.name: V Projection Rail
parts.role: Copper rail separates the value projection before cache write and attention readback.

parts.name: 96 Query-Head Fanout Comb
parts.role: Wide comb represents Q projection to 96 heads of 128 channels each.

parts.name: 8 KV-Head Bank
parts.role: Narrow bank represents K and V projection to only 8 grouped-query heads, a 12:1 sharing ratio against Q.
parts.flops_per_token: about 2 x d x 2 x 8 x 128
parts.algorithm: K = x @ W_K; V = x @ W_V

parts.name: QK-Norm Disk
parts.role: Flat disk marks per-head RMSNorm applied to Q and K before the attention dot product.

parts.name: Partial RoPE Half-Channel Ring
parts.role: Torus marks rotary position encoding applied to 64 of each 128 head channels.
parts.algorithm: rotate the first 64 QK channels by position

parts.name: Half-Channel RoPE Mask
parts.role: Thin mask bar blocks half the RoPE ring to show that only half of each attention head is rotated.

parts.name: FlashAttention-2 Core
parts.role: Dense causal FlashAttention core streams Q, K, and V tiles through SRAM without storing the full attention matrix.
parts.algorithm: attn = softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_h)); out = attn @ V

parts.name: Attention O-Projection Plate
parts.role: Output projection plate maps concatenated attention heads back to d=5120 before residual addition.

parts.name: Attention Residual Return Bus
parts.role: Horizontal bus shows the attention output being added back into the central residual pipe.

parts.name: KV Cache Manifold
parts.role: Vertical manifold collects the eight GQA KV cache cartridges for prefill writes and decode reads.
parts.memory_footprint: about 2 KB per token per layer at 8 KV heads and FP8
parts.bottleneck: HBM capacity sets max batchable context per GPU.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 1
parts.role: First visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 2
parts.role: Second visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 3
parts.role: Third visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 4
parts.role: Fourth visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 5
parts.role: Fifth visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 6
parts.role: Sixth visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 7
parts.role: Seventh visible KV-head cache cell stores one grouped K/V head lane.

parts.name: KV Cache Cell 8
parts.role: Eighth visible KV-head cache cell completes the 8-head GQA cache set.

parts.name: FFN Post-Attention RMSNorm Plate
parts.role: RMSNorm plate normalizes the residual stream before the sparse MoE feed-forward sublayer.
parts.algorithm: x_hat = x / sqrt(mean(x*x) + eps); y = gamma * x_hat

parts.name: Top-8 Sigmoid Router
parts.role: Router disk scores 160 experts with sigmoid gates and selects the top eight experts per token.
parts.memory_footprint: W_router is about 1.6 MB per layer BF16
parts.algorithm: scores = sigmoid(x @ W_router) + b_balance; topk = topk(scores, 8)
parts.bottleneck: Router is sequential with the following all-to-all dispatch.

parts.name: Top-K Token Bead 1
parts.role: First token bead visualizes the routed token leaving the sigmoid router.

parts.name: Top-K Token Bead 2
parts.role: Second token bead shows the selected top-k path crossing the group limiter.

parts.name: Top-K Token Bead 3
parts.role: Third token bead marks bounded dispatch into the all-to-all ring.

parts.name: Top-K Token Bead 4
parts.role: Fourth token bead enters the expert dispatch ring before fanning to selected experts.

parts.name: Group-Limited Routing Ring
parts.role: Ring enforces the rule that a token may activate experts in no more than four of eight device groups.
parts.algorithm: skip expert e if group(e) would exceed the 4-group budget

parts.name: Expert All-to-All Dispatch Ring
parts.role: Dispatch ring represents the NCCL all-to-all that buckets tokens by selected expert before grouped GEMM.
parts.bottleneck: Cross-node InfiniBand traffic and skew-induced stragglers.

parts.name: Curved Eight-Group Expert Backplane
parts.role: Curved backplane places the eight device groups around the all-to-all path instead of a flat rectangular rack.

parts.name: Expert Arc Front Support Post
parts.role: Front support post visibly carries the curved expert bank down to the right frame rail.

parts.name: Expert Arc Rear Support Post
parts.role: Rear support post stabilizes the curved expert bank and prevents the cartridges from reading as floating blocks.

parts.name: Expert Group 1 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 of the 160 routed experts for expert-parallel placement.

parts.name: Expert Group 2 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts and can be one of the four allowed groups for a token.

parts.name: Expert Group 3 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts and exposes the MoE bank as separate hardware lanes.

parts.name: Expert Group 4 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts and completes the typical four-group budget example.

parts.name: Expert Group 5 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts that remain available but may be skipped by the group limiter.

parts.name: Expert Group 6 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts and shows that the full bank spans eight groups.

parts.name: Expert Group 7 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds 20 routed experts and provides a visible inactive contrast to the selected lanes.

parts.name: Expert Group 8 Cartridge
parts.role: Device-group cartridge holds the final 20 routed experts in the 160-expert MoE layer.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 1
parts.role: Highlighted lane shows one of the eight top-k routed expert calls for the current token.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 2
parts.role: Highlighted lane shows a second top-k expert call sharing the grouped GEMM bed.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 3
parts.role: Highlighted lane shows a third selected expert in the top-8 dispatch set.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 4
parts.role: Highlighted lane shows the fourth selected expert group allowed by the group limiter.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 5
parts.role: Highlighted lane shows the fifth top-k expert call routed from the second half of the arc.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 6
parts.role: Highlighted lane shows the sixth routed expert call entering the shared grouped GEMM bed.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 7
parts.role: Highlighted lane shows the seventh selected expert call in the top-8 MoE path.

parts.name: Active Expert Lane 8
parts.role: Highlighted lane completes the eight routed expert calls selected for one token.

parts.name: 160-Routed-Expert Count Comb
parts.role: Comb spine marks eight groups of twenty routed experts so the 160-expert count is visible beside the arc.

parts.name: Expert Count Tick Group 1
parts.role: Tick marks the first group of twenty routed experts in the selected half of the bank.

parts.name: Expert Count Tick Group 2
parts.role: Tick marks the second group of twenty routed experts in the selected half of the bank.

parts.name: Expert Count Tick Group 3
parts.role: Tick marks the third group of twenty routed experts in the selected half of the bank.

parts.name: Expert Count Tick Group 4
parts.role: Tick marks the fourth group of twenty routed experts allowed by the group limiter.

parts.name: Expert Count Tick Group 5
parts.role: Tick marks the fifth group of twenty routed experts in the full bank.

parts.name: Expert Count Tick Group 6
parts.role: Tick marks the sixth group of twenty routed experts in the full bank.

parts.name: Expert Count Tick Group 7
parts.role: Tick marks the seventh group of twenty routed experts in the full bank.

parts.name: Expert Count Tick Group 8
parts.role: Tick marks the eighth group of twenty routed experts, completing the 160-routed-expert count.

parts.name: Shared Expert Always-On Block
parts.role: Always-on shared expert carries common computation in parallel with the eight routed experts.

parts.name: Grouped GEMM Expert Bed
parts.role: Grouped GEMM bed fuses capacity-padded SwiGLU expert matrix multiplications into one kernel launch.
parts.flops_per_token: about 350 MFLOP per active MoE layer
parts.memory_footprint: 160 x 3 x 5120 x 1408 x BF16 is about 11 GiB per layer
parts.algorithm: H = silu(X @ W_gate) * (X @ W_up); O = H @ W_down

parts.name: FP8 GEMM Precision Disk
parts.role: Precision marker shows FP8 E4M3 forward and E5M2 backward GEMMs with BF16 master weights.
parts.memory_footprint: FP8 forward weights are about two times smaller than BF16.

parts.name: Expert All-to-All Combine Ring
parts.role: Combine ring represents the return all-to-all that sends expert outputs back to their original token order.
parts.bottleneck: Cross-node combine latency can stall the residual update.

parts.name: MoE Residual Return Bus
parts.role: Return bus carries the combined MoE output back into the central residual pipe.

parts.name: LM Head Left Vocabulary Slab
parts.role: Left half of the tied output projection maps final hidden states back to the 151,552-token vocabulary while leaving the residual pipe visible.

parts.name: LM Head Right Vocabulary Slab
parts.role: Right half of the tied output projection completes the vocabulary GEMM without forming an opaque cap over the stack.

parts.name: Tied LM Head Bridge Bus
parts.role: Small bridge shows the left and right vocabulary shards are one tied LM head rather than separate classifiers.

parts.name: MTP Head Depth 1
parts.role: Single multi-token-prediction head supplies speculative decoding targets for about 1.8 times inference speedup.
parts.flops_per_token: about one extra block plus LM head GEMM

parts.name: MTP Head Support Post
parts.role: Slender post visibly supports the elevated MTP head from the right rail.

parts.name: Primary Cross-Entropy Loss
parts.role: Primary next-token cross-entropy loss node supervises the tied LM head during training.

parts.name: Primary Loss Support Rod
parts.role: Short rod ties the primary loss node mechanically back to the LM head bracket.

parts.name: Auxiliary MTP Loss
parts.role: Small auxiliary loss trains the MTP head to predict an additional future token.

parts.name: MTP Loss Support Rod
parts.role: Short rod ties the auxiliary MTP loss node back to the MTP head frame.

parts.name: Think Mode Selector
parts.role: Mode plate represents system-prompt selection for chain-of-thought reasoning with a larger decode budget.

parts.name: No-Think Mode Selector
parts.role: Mode plate represents direct-answer prompting that shares weights but uses a smaller reasoning budget.

parts.name: Shared Weight Mode Selector Bus
parts.role: Bus ties both think and no-think plates back to the same LM head to show shared weights.

parts.name: 23T-Token Curriculum Feed
parts.role: Data feed plate represents about 23 trillion tokens across general, reasoning, and long-context training stages.

parts.name: General Pretraining Stage Plate
parts.role: Small plate marks the first broad general-text stage of the 23T-token curriculum.

parts.name: Reasoning Curriculum Stage Plate
parts.role: Small plate marks the second reasoning-heavy pretraining stage.

parts.name: Long-Context Stage Plate
parts.role: Small plate marks the long-context extension stage that supports 128K context.

parts.name: AdamW Optimizer Station
parts.role: Optimizer station stores Adam moments and BF16 master weights for the full 355B-parameter model.
parts.memory_footprint: Adam state stores m and v, roughly two times parameter size before sharding.
parts.algorithm: m = beta1*m + (1-beta1)*g; v = beta2*v + (1-beta2)*g*g; W -= lr*mhat/(sqrt(vhat)+eps)

parts.name: Optimizer Support Post
parts.role: Support post anchors the elevated optimizer station to the base frame so it no longer floats.

parts.name: Loss-to-Optimizer Gradient Bus
parts.role: Long bus carries primary and MTP loss gradients down to the AdamW optimizer station.

parts.name: Self-Distillation RL Station
parts.role: Post-training station represents SFT plus self-distillation RL rollouts for agentic, reasoning, and coding tasks.
parts.algorithm: rollouts = sample(policy, prompts); rewards = score(rollouts); loss = grpo_loss(rollouts, rewards)

parts.name: Post-Training Support Arm
parts.role: Short vertical arm bolts the RL station directly above the optimizer station.

parts.name: Parallelism Board Support Post
parts.role: Outboard support post carries the TP, EP, PP, and DP parallelism board from the right frame rail.

parts.name: TP x EP x PP x DP Parallelism Board
parts.role: Parallelism board maps tensor, expert, pipeline, and data parallel axes onto the visible attention, MoE, layer, and optimizer modules.
parts.algorithm: rank = (dp, pp, ep, tp); experts assigned by EP group; layers split across PP stages

parts.name: Tensor Parallel Axis Bar
parts.role: Axis bar marks tensor parallelism on attention and vocabulary GEMM shards.

parts.name: Expert Parallel Axis Bar
parts.role: Axis bar marks expert parallelism on the MoE all-to-all and expert cartridge bank.

parts.name: Pipeline Parallel Axis Bar
parts.role: Axis bar marks pipeline parallelism along the 96-layer vertical stack.

parts.name: Data Parallel Axis Bar
parts.role: Axis bar marks data parallelism on losses, optimizer state, and post-training rollout batches.
